// @path: src/lib/ops/operations.ts
// @expect: OPS-MODEL-METHOD
// The WRITE half of the SchoolInvitation classification (ruling R2). Its
// sibling bad-ops-lists-school-invitations.txt proves the browse is refused.
//
// SchoolInvitation is LOOKUP_ONLY — findUnique, findUniqueOrThrow, count, and
// nothing else — so this fixture is refused for the strictest available reason:
// not "delete is missing from an otherwise generous list", but "no write of any
// shape is permitted on this model at all". It would fire identically for
// create, update, updateMany or upsert.
//
// Deliberately placed in the ONE module permitted to mutate anything, so that
// OPS-MUTATION-MODULE cannot fire and the CLASSIFICATION is what refuses it.
// Written at src/lib/ops/reads.ts this fixture would pass for the wrong reason
// and prove nothing about the method list.
//
// The near miss the model invites: "tidying up" a stale offer from a support
// call. Deleting the row is how the history of who asked whom disappears —
// and this codebase keeps history in the audit log, not by leaving rows lying
// about, so a support fix that removes the record removes the wrong thing. The
// state vocabulary already has REVOKED for a school taking an offer back, and
// that is a write an admin makes on their own console, not an operator.
import { db } from "@/lib/db";

export async function tidyStaleInvitation(invitationId) {
  return db.schoolInvitation.delete({ where: { id: invitationId } });
}
